newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania Bancorex "normal" after boss sacked.
newsitem.headline: Romania Bancorex "normal" after boss sacked.

text.p: Romania's leading state-run bank Bancorex SA, whose former boss was sacked and investigated by police at the weekend, said on Monday its activity was "normal".
"The activity of the bank runs in normal circumstances," the Banca Romana de Comert Exterior Bancorex SA said in a statement.
It was Bancorex's first official statement since a shareholders' meeting decided last Friday to sack former bank chairman Razvan Temesan and replace him with Florin Ionescu.
No run on the bank's branches in Bucharest or across the country was reported on Monday.
Temesan was interviewed by police for several hours last Friday and eventually released but barred from leaving Bucharest for the next 30 days.
The Interior Ministry said in a statement a special police committee was investigating alleged irregularities committed by Temesan as a member of Bancorex's board.
Temesan denied the allegations, saying his removal last Friday had been a "coup".
The central bank also confirmed last Friday that Bancorex remained a "solid" bank despite its management shake-up.
Bancorex specialised in foreign trade financing, handles the bulk of foreign exchange trading on the local market.
It is one of the favourite commercial banks among Romania's population because of its attractive deposit rates, amounting to an annual 150 percent on one-month funds.
